Let

\[
Q_{p,s}(c)=\sum_{z,w\in Y}c_zc_w d_s(z,w)^p,\qquad \sum_z c_z=0.
\]

For \(s<0\), all three added chords are longer than the corresponding old shortest paths, so the metric is locally constant and equals \(d_0\). Hence \(\wp'(0^-)=0\) once \(\wp(0)\) is known.

At \(s=0\), the metric embeds isometrically into \(\ell_1\): put

\[
\ast=0,\quad a_1=e_1,\quad a_3=e_2,\quad a_2=e_1+e_2,
\]
\[
b_1=e_3,\quad b_3=e_4,\quad b_2=e_3+e_4.
\]

Thus \(d_0\) has \(1\)-negative type, and therefore \(p\)-negative type for every \(0<p\le 1\).

To see that \(p>1\) immediately fails, use the zero-sum vector

\[
c_{a_1}=c_{a_3}=1,\quad c_{a_2}=-1,\quad
c_{b_1}=c_{b_3}=-1,\quad c_{b_2}=1,\quad c_\ast=0.
\]

Writing \(q=2^p,\ r=3^p\), one obtains

\[
Q_{p,0}(c)=-4q-8+8r-2q^2.
\]

At \(p=1\) this is \(0\), while

\[
\frac{d}{dp}Q_{p,0}(c)\bigg|_{p=1}
=24\log 3-24\log 2
=24\log\frac32>0.
\]

So \(Q_{p,0}(c)>0\) for \(p>1\) close to \(1\), and hence

\[
\wp(0)=1.
\]

Now take \(s>0\). The only distances changing to first order are

\[
d_s(a_1,a_3)=2-s,\qquad d_s(b_1,b_3)=2-2s,\qquad d_s(a_2,b_2)=4-s.
\]

At \((p,s)=(1,0)\), the kernel of \(Q_{1,0}\) on \(\sum c_z=0\) is two-dimensional. Write its elements as

\[
c=m v+n w,
\]

where

\[
v=(-2;\ 1,-1,1;\ 1,-1,1),
\]
\[
w=(0;\ 1,-1,1;\ -1,1,-1),
\]

with entries ordered as \(\ast; a_1,a_2,a_3; b_1,b_2,b_3\).

For this kernel,

\[
\partial_p Q_{p,0}(c)\big|_{p=1}
=2U m^2+2V n^2,
\]

where

\[
U=4\log\frac{128}{27},\qquad V=12\log\frac32.
\]

Also,

\[
\partial_s Q_{1,s}(c)\big|_{s=0^+}
=-8m^2+4mn-4n^2.
\]

Therefore if \(p=1+\alpha s+o(s)\), the first-order kernel form is

\[
(2U\alpha-8)m^2+4mn+(2V\alpha-4)n^2.
\]

The threshold occurs when this quadratic form is negative semidefinite with zero determinant:

\[
(2U\alpha-8)(2V\alpha-4)-4=0.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
UV\alpha^2-(2U+4V)\alpha+7=0.
\]

The smaller root gives the right derivative:

\[
\alpha=\frac{U+2V-\sqrt{U^2-3UV+4V^2}}{UV}.
\]

Hence

\[
\boxed{
\left(
1,\,
0,\,
\frac{U+2V-\sqrt{U^2-3UV+4V^2}}{UV}
\right)
}.
\]
